findings.claim: Beyond the elastic limit, the graph curves upwards - this is the non-linear region where Hooke's Law no longer applies.
findings.truth: On the force-extension graph the lesson itself specifies (force on the y-axis, extension on the x-axis), the line bends TOWARDS the extension axis beyond the elastic limit: the gradient falls, because each extra newton now produces a bigger extension. Saying it curves upwards would lose the mark on any graph-shape question.
findings.evidence: spec P2.3c and P2.3d (force-extension graph, linear and non-linear relationships); the same lesson's practical, narration n11, tells students to plot force on the y-axis against extension on the x-axis

findings.claim: The whole Gas Pressure and Temperature section sits inside a div class="higher-only" wrapper.
findings.truth: Gas pressure and its link to temperature are assessed at BOTH tiers. Neither statement is bold in the spec, so the wrapper hides required content from Foundation students. Wrapper removed (opening and closing tag).
findings.evidence: bold spec P1.2g and P1.2h are in plain type; the topic P1.2 tiering note says only bold statements are Higher Tier only

findings.claim: The equation v^2 = u^2 + 2as sits inside a div class="higher-only" wrapper.
findings.truth: This equation is assessed at both tiers in J250. It appears in plain type in the Select and apply table, so it is given on the equation sheet but is NOT Higher-tier only. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: bold spec PM2.1iii, plain type, listed under 'Learners are expected to select and apply the following equations'

findings.claim: The Energy Stored in a Spring section (elastic potential energy, half k e squared) sits inside a div class="higher-only" wrapper.
findings.truth: Elastic potential energy is assessed at both tiers. P2.3f (calculate the work done in stretching) and PM2.3ii are both in plain type. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: bold spec P2.3f and PM2.3ii, both plain type

findings.claim: The area under a velocity-time graph is correctly wrapped as higher-only in the article, but a practice question, a knowledge check, a flashcard and a key takeaway all test it with no tier flag.
findings.truth: Interpreting enclosed areas in velocity-time graphs is bold, so it is tested only in the Higher Tier papers. '(Higher tier)' prefix added to the question and knowledge check, tag appended to the flashcard question, and the takeaway re-worded.

findings.claim: Terminal velocity, momentum, conservation of momentum and inertia are correctly wrapped as higher-only in the article, but two practice questions, one knowledge check, three flashcards and a key takeaway test them with no tier flag.
findings.truth: All four are bold statements, tested only in the Higher Tier papers. Tier tags added.
findings.evidence: bold spec P2.2f, P2.2j, P2.2k and PM2.2ii (all bold)

findings.claim: The motor effect, F = BIl, Fleming's left-hand rule and electric motors are correctly wrapped as higher-only in the article, but three practice questions, three knowledge checks, four flashcards, the key takeaway and the whole exam tip test them with no tier flag.
findings.truth: P3.3h to P3.3k and the force-on-a-conductor equation are all bold, so they are tested only in the Higher Tier papers. Tier tags added.
findings.evidence: bold spec P3.3h, P3.3i, P3.3j, P3.3k and PM3.3i (all bold)

findings.claim: Flashcard: 'Name one element that is strongly magnetic.' Answer: 'Iron, steel, nickel or cobalt.'
findings.truth: Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon, not an element, and the question asks for one element. Answer changed to 'Iron.'
findings.evidence: settled fact; spec P3.3 requires magnetic materials only, and the validator rejects a short flashcard answer written as a list

findings.claim: Description is 117 characters: 'AC and DC current, mains wiring safety, electrical power, energy transfer, and the National Grid transmission system.'
findings.truth: The house limit is under 100 characters, and 'AC and DC current' repeats the word current (alternating current current). Shortened to 87 characters.

findings.claim: Eighteen flashcard answers in all eight lessons carry raw LaTeX or caret notation in plain-text fields: \rho, \Delta, \times, \Omega, \tfrac{1}{2}, E_p, E_e, m/s^2, kg/m^3, I^2, v^2, u^2.
findings.truth: Flashcards render as text, so a student literally reads '\Delta Q = m \times c \times \Delta \theta'. All rewritten with unicode characters. L2 also used Q for thermal energy where the spec writes change in thermal energy (E) and E = m l.
findings.evidence: house convention: plain-text fields use unicode, only *_html fields carry markup; spec equation tables PM1.2i, PM1.2ii

findings.claim: Flashcard answer: '9 m (using s = \tfrac{1}{2} a t^2).'
findings.truth: The answer is numerically right (u = 0, a = 2, t = 3 gives 9 m) but s = half a t squared is on neither the recall list nor the equation sheet for J250. Recomputed by the in-spec route: average speed is 3 m/s over 3 s, so s = 9 m. Raw LaTeX also removed.
findings.evidence: spec equation lists 5g: recall-and-apply and select-and-apply tables contain no s = half a t squared

findings.claim: Lesson 7 teaches the National Grid, step-up and step-down transformers, the transformer equation, a.c. versus d.c., 230 V / 50 Hz mains and the live, neutral and earth wires as part of a Physics Paper 1 unit.
findings.truth: All of that is Topic P6 Global challenges, which the spec examines on Physics Paper 2 (Foundation Paper 6 / Higher Paper 12). Physics Paper 1 (Foundation Paper 5 / Higher Paper 11) covers only P1 Matter, P2 Forces and P3 Electricity and magnetism, plus CS7 practical skills. Only the power and energy content of lesson 7 (P = VI, P = I squared R, E = Pt, kW h and cost) belongs to Paper 1, via P3.2. Ruling: the lesson stays where it is and carries a scope label instead. A one-line scope note is inserted straight after the Mains Wiring and Safety heading, the first point in the lesson where the Paper 2 material starts, telling students that the national grid, transformers and mains wiring are examined on Paper 2.
findings.evidence: spec section 2a paper mapping, and bold spec P6.2c to P6.2i plus PM6.2i

findings.claim: Lesson 7 teaches and assesses fuses and residual current devices: practice question 4 asks students to suggest a fuse rating, the earth-wire mark scheme depends on the fuse blowing, the exam tip gives a fuse-rating rule, and two flashcards test fuses and RCDs.
findings.truth: Neither 'fuse' nor 'residual current device' appears anywhere in the J250 specification. The nearest statement, P6.2i, extends only to 'the protection offered by insulation of devices'. The physics as written is correct, so nothing is misleading, but no J250 question can require it and the fuse-rating question cannot appear on any paper. Options: keep it as background safety knowledge (it is genuinely useful and correct), or replace practice question 4 with a P = VI question that stays in scope. Recommend replacing practice question 4 only, and leaving the prose.
findings.evidence: grep of the whole spec for fuse, residual current, plug: only P6.2h 'Wiring of a plug' and P6.2i insulation appear

findings.claim: Coverage gaps: three both-tier statements in P1 to P3 are taught nowhere in the unit.
findings.truth: P2.2c (represent forces as vectors, including drawing free body force diagrams) is missing entirely, and so are the Higher statements built on it - P2.2e (resolution of forces and equilibrium), P2.2g and P2.2h (resultant and balanced forces from free body diagrams). P3.2b (represent d.c. circuits with the standard symbols for cells, power supply, diodes, LDRs, NTC thermistors, filament lamps, ammeter, voltmeter, fixed and variable resistors and switch) is named nowhere; lesson 6 names the components but never the symbols. Recommend a new lesson or a new section in lesson 4 on free body force diagrams, and a circuit-symbols section in lesson 6. Everything else in P1.1, P1.2, P2.1, P2.3, P3.1, P3.2 and P3.3 is covered.
findings.evidence: bold spec statements P2.2c, P2.2e, P2.2g, P2.2h and P3.2b checked against all eight lessons

findings.truth: The eight lessons map exactly onto P1 Matter (lessons 1-2), P2 Forces (lessons 3-5) and P3 Electricity and magnetism (lessons 6-8), which is Foundation Paper 5 / Higher Paper 11 - correct for a Physics Paper 1 unit, apart from the P6 content noted in F12. Note for the tracker: the briefing anchor 'Paper 1 covers P1-P4 (Matter; Forces; Electricity; Magnetism)' does not hold for J250. In this specification P3 is one topic, 'Electricity and magnetism', and P4 is 'Waves and radioactivity', which sits on Paper 2. No lesson makes any claim about paper count, duration or marks, so there is nothing to correct in the content.
findings.evidence: spec section 2a, Foundation and Higher assessment overviews: six papers, each 1 hour 10 minutes, 60 marks, 16.7 per cent

findings.claim: Lesson 3 teaches, in unwrapped prose and an unwrapped key fact, that an object moving in a circle at constant speed has a changing velocity and is always accelerating.
findings.truth: P2.2p is bold, so this is Higher-tier-only material. It is not wrong, and it illustrates the both-tier vector-scalar statement P2.1d well, so removing it or wrapping it would hurt Foundation students more than it helps. Recommend leaving the prose as it stands. The flashcard that drills the statement directly has been tagged (Higher tier).

findings.claim: 'This is why the National Grid is efficient - only about 2% of energy is lost in transmission.'
findings.truth: About 2 per cent is right for the high-voltage transmission network, which is what the sentence says. Total transmission plus distribution losses in the UK are nearer 8 per cent, so the figure would be wrong if a student quoted it for the whole journey to the home. Not worth an edit, but worth knowing if the sentence is ever reused.
findings.evidence: settled fact; the spec gives no figure

findings.claim: Lesson 6 ends by saying LDRs and thermistors are used in potential divider circuits.
findings.truth: Potential dividers are not named anywhere in J250. The sentence is correct physics and is a single passing mention, so it is harmless extension. No edit.
findings.evidence: grep of the spec: potential divider does not appear; P3.2f and P3.2k cover circuit design in general terms

summary: Eight lessons checked against OCR Combined Science A Gateway J250. Every worked example, mark-scheme calculation and knowledge-check key recomputed correct, including g = 10 N/kg, which is the value this spec states. One HIGH physics error (force-extension graph shape, lesson 5). The wrapper fault runs both ways: three higher-only wrappers hid both-tier content (gas pressure, v squared minus u squared = 2as, elastic potential energy) and were removed, while the five correct wrappers were kept and the questions, flashcards and takeaways that test that same bold content were tagged (Higher tier). Eighteen flashcard answers carried raw LaTeX that students read literally. Two scope issues need Tom's ruling: lesson 7 teaches Paper 2 content (national grid, transformers, mains wiring) plus out-of-spec fuses and RCDs, and free body force diagrams (P2.2c) and circuit symbols (P3.2b) are taught nowhere. 56 edits.
